html:
The Old Bazaar of Skopje is the old market quarter of the city on the left bank of the Vardar River, which grew into one of the largest bazaars in the Balkans under Ottoman rule from the 1400s.

Its narrow streets held craft guilds, inns for caravans, baths and mosques, among them the Mustafa Pasha Mosque of 1492 and the Daut Pasha Hammam. It was the trading heart of a crossroads town on routes between the Adriatic, Thessaloniki and the Danube. A stone bridge over the Vardar linked it to the other bank. The bazaar burned in 1689 when an Austrian army set fire to Skopje during the Great Turkish War, and it was damaged again in the 1963 earthquake, but much of it survives in North Macedonia's capital.
sum: The Old Bazaar of Skopje is the old market quarter of the city on the left bank of the Vardar River, which grew into one of the largest bazaars in the Balkans under Ottoman rule from the 1400s.
